title: model-admittance-surge-mitigation-heatmap-and-backing-cache-estimate
content:
Summary:
This planning sheet estimates the immediate and 30-day infrastructure impact for admitting a new large-reasoning model (codename: lighthouse-v1) into the hosted fleet. Focus areas: regional GPU slot pressure, backing KV cache occupancy per region, eviction risk, tail latency sensitivity, and a staged admittance plan with throttle knobs. This is intentionally conservative and meant to produce an actionable heatmap for ops during the soft-admit window.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Model: lighthouse-v1 (dense 70B, KV-friendly checkpoint, 16-bit activations, supports quantized variants).
- Avg request distribution: 60% short chat (avg_seq_len=512 tokens), 30% long chat (avg_seq_len=4096), 10% batch embeddings/other.
- Token generation speed per A100-80GB equivalent slot: 4800 tokens/s (inference + attention).
- Avg tokens generated per request: 150 (post-continuation trimming); generation fraction applied to QPS below.
- KV per session: base KV entries = 48 (per conversation), mean entry size=680 bytes -> ~32.6 KB/session live footprint.
- TTL policy (proposed during soft admit): 1.5 hours active, 12h cold linger.
- Active concurrency headroom target: reserve 15% fleet for control-plane/system traffic.

Fleet baseline (slots = model-constrained slots available for lighthouse-v1; these are slots that pass binary/compat with quantized variant fallback):
- us-west-2: 1,220 slots
- us-east-1: 930 slots
- europe-west: 610 slots
- apac-east: 290 slots
- global-total: 3,050 slots

Projected per-slot admission capacity (concurrency):
- Average active sessions per slot (with batching): 18 sessions/slot at target latency SLO (p95 generation latency 400ms).
- Effective sessions supported = slots * sessions/slot * (1 - reserve). Example: us-west-2 effective = 1,220 * 18 * 0.85 = ~18,666 sessions.

KV cache footprint calc (active working set):
- KV/session ~32.6 KB -> active working set per region = effective_sessions * 32.6KB
- us-west-2 active KV bytes = 18,666 * 32.6KB = ~608 GB active (rounded)
- us-east-1 = 14,220 sessions * 32.6KB = ~465 GB
- europe-west = 9,333 sessions * 32.6KB = ~305 GB
- apac-east = 4,443 sessions * 32.6KB = ~145 GB
- Total active KV working set ~1.52 TB (active set across regions)

Backing cache + cold store needs:
- Cold linger (12h) significantly increases stored KV but does not occupy hot memory. Estimated cold store delta ~x8 active (worst-case) due to historical chat re-entry patterns and missed evictions -> ~12 TB of backing store required across regions during soft admit.

Eviction risk and frag sensitivity:
- Heap fragmentation and model-specific KV stripe sizes create a non-linear eviction curve. If hot RAM allocation per host falls below 20% free, eviction rate jumps and p95 latency penalty increases ~2.8x.
- Current observed eviction threshold: hot-cache occupancy > 78% correlates with degraded tail (observed on smaller rollouts).

Simulation snapshots (deterministic sim with sampled QPS patterns):
Scenario A — Controlled soft-admit (recommended starter):
- Admission schedule: day0 5% of global QPS -> day1 15% -> day3 35% -> day7 60% -> day14 85% -> day30 100%
- Peak regional GPU util at day7: us-west-2 73%, us-east-1 69%, europe-west 62%, apac-east 55%
- Hot KV occupancy at day7: us-west-2 52% hot RAM reserved for KV, eviction rate low (<0.2% per 10s window)
- Estimated tail p95 generation latency increase: +12% over baseline

Scenario B — Aggressive admit (not recommended):
- Admission at 40% global QPS on day0 -> results: us-west-2 util > 92% (critical), hot KV > 84% -> eviction events, retries cascade, p99 latency spikes 3-6x.

Scenario C — Regional-first phased admit (safe for mixed loads):
- Start in europe-west + apac-east at 20% region-specific QPS while holding US regions at 0%; after 72h, ramp US to 30%
- Benefit: Europe/APAC hot-cache stays under 65%, US admits later with additional pre-warm measures.

Heatmap (operational):
- Colors driven by combined metric = max(gpu_util_pct, hot_kv_pct * 1.1) to bias toward cache pressure.
- Thresholds: green < 65%, yellow 65-80%, orange 80-90%, red >90%
- Day7 estimated heatmap: us-west-2 -> yellow/orange (73% gpu, 52% cache -> effective 57% -> yellow), us-east-1 -> yellow, europe-west -> green, apac-east -> green.

Immediate mitigation knobs (short-term, actionable):
1) Soft-admit queueing: enforce global QPS cap for lighthouse-v1 by tier. Start with tier-0 (internal) 100% allowed, tier-1 (paid) 25% of normal quota.
2) Concurrency throttle per-API-key: limit to 6 concurrent sessions per key for first 72h.
3) Reserve slots per region: pin 12% additional slots as "warm-only" for control-plane and pre-warm operations (over the 15% baseline reserve).
4) Reduce KV TTL to 45 minutes for users flagged as low-activity during first week to reduce hot working set pressure.
5) Deploy quantized fallback binary for long tails to reduce tokens/s by ~1.6x for non-latency critical customers.
6) Introduce short-lived pre-warm synthetic traffic (2 RPS per region per model) routed to warm-only slots to seed KV with high-probability prefixes.

Operational checklist (owners + ETA):
- Capacity: run per-host KV memory scan + fragmentation report (owner: Ethan Li, ETA: 2026-01-15)
- Quota: implement temporary per-key concurrency limit in API gateway (owner: Priya Nambiar, ETA: 2026-01-14)
- Observability: add 'lighthouse-v1' breakdown to per-route cost/latency dashboard and heatmap overlay (owner: Samir Khatri, ETA: 2026-01-13)
- Rollout coordination: schedule canary in europe-west for 2026-01-20 before global ramp (owner: Marta Ruiz, ETA: 2026-01-18)

Follow-ups and experiments to reduce uncertainty:
- Experiment 1: KV entry compression (gzip-lite) to test 20-30% working set reduction on 10k sampled sessions. (owner: storage team, 2-week A/B)
- Experiment 2: Adaptive TTL based on re-entry probability per user segment; measure hit-rate and tail latency impact. (owner: product-hosted-api, 3 weeks)
- Experiment 3: Shard-aware KV placement: colocate hot prefixes with model-serving pods to reduce cross-host pressure (owner: infra/placement team, spike 1 week)

Risks and open questions:
- Backing-store capacity estimate for cold linger is highly sensitive to user re-entry behavior; if 24h re-entry > 12%, backing-store could exceed 20 TB during initial ramp. Need S3 bucket lifecycle and cost check.
- Quantized fallback may reduce quality for some customers — need product sign-off and an automated rollback path.
- Cross-region failover: if US regions degrade, rerouting to EU could overload EU quickly. Set cross-region guardrails in router.

Appendix A: Quick math snippets
- Effective_sessions(region) = slots * sessions_per_slot * (1 - reserve_pct)
- Active_KV_GB = Effective_sessions * KV_session_bytes / 1024^3
- Hot_cache_pct = Active_KV_GB / total_hot_ram_allocated_to_kv_in_region

Appendix B: Baseline telemetry checks to signal rollback (automated alarms recommended)
- sustained gpu_util > 90% for 5m OR hot_cache_pct > 80% for 2m -> auto-throttle 30% incoming QPS for new-model route
- p99 generation latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes -> immediate canary freeze and rollback to previous model

Notes:
- This sheet purposefully focuses on the "first 30 days" soft-admit behavior and hot KV memory pressure. Long-term steady-state cost/slot efficiency and quantization experiments belong to the Optimize backlog.
- All numbers are rounded and should be recalculated with real traffic samples during the canary window.

End of sheet.
